providers.name: Harbor House Community Services
providers.audience: Adults experiencing homelessness or at risk of losing housing.
providers.services: Day shelter, meals, showers, laundry, mail access, housing navigation, and referrals for overnight shelter.
providers.access: Visit the Harbor House public day-center reception and ask for a housing navigator. Tell them whether you need somewhere to stay tonight.

providers.name: Family Bridge of Stapleton
providers.audience: Families with children who need stable housing.
providers.services: Family shelter intake, housing case management, help keeping families together, and links to childcare and school support.
providers.access: Ask the Family Bridge intake desk for a family housing assessment; explain how many adults and children need shelter.

providers.name: Willow Haven Survivor Services
providers.audience: People affected by domestic or dating violence, sexual assault, or coercive control, including women and their children.
providers.services: Confidential advocacy, safety planning, emergency shelter screening, court accompaniment, and support groups. Survivors of any gender can request help.
providers.access: Ask for an advocate at the public Willow Haven advocacy office. Shelter locations are not public. You do not need to describe the abuse in this chat.
providers.hours: Public advocacy-office walk-ins: Monday–Friday, 9 AM–5 PM.

providers.name: Open Door Recovery Network
providers.audience: Adults seeking help with alcohol or other drug use, and family members looking for support.
providers.services: Treatment navigation, screening referrals, connections to licensed outpatient or residential treatment, and insurance or payment-resource guidance.
providers.access: Ask the Open Door intake desk for a treatment-navigation conversation. Ask specifically about medically supervised withdrawal care if that is what you need.

providers.name: Next Step Peer Collective
providers.audience: People in recovery or considering a change in substance use.
providers.services: Peer recovery coaching, support groups, practical goal planning, and harm-reduction education. This is peer support, not a medical detox facility.
providers.access: Visit the Next Step community room and ask about a peer navigator or the current group schedule.

providers.name: Stapleton Community Table
providers.audience: Households that need groceries or cannot cover both food and basic expenses.
providers.services: Choice-based grocery pantry, hygiene supplies when stocked, and help finding food-benefit application support.
providers.access: Visit the Community Table pantry welcome desk. No photo ID or proof of income is required; staff ask household size to plan groceries.
providers.hours: Pantry shopping: Tuesday and Thursday, noon–6 PM; Saturday, 10 AM–1 PM.

providers.name: Neighbor’s Kitchen
providers.services: Free prepared community meals and information about other food resources.
providers.access: Come to the Neighbor’s Kitchen meal hall during serving hours. No registration is required.

providers.name: Bright Beginnings Community Action
providers.audience: Families seeking early childhood education and family support.
providers.services: Head Start for children ages 3–5 and Early Head Start for pregnant people and children under 3; developmental screenings, family support, and enrollment assistance.
providers.access: Ask the Bright Beginnings enrollment office for an eligibility review and current application checklist. Income and other eligibility rules apply; enrollment depends on an available place.

providers.name: Stapleton Autism and Family Resource Center
providers.audience: Autistic children and adults, people seeking evaluation information, and families or caregivers.
providers.services: Autism information, family navigation, sensory-friendly activities, peer groups, and referrals to licensed assessment and therapy providers.
providers.access: Ask the resource-center welcome desk for a family or adult-services navigator. A diagnosis is not required for an initial information conversation.

providers.name: Common Ground Disability Alliance
providers.audience: People with developmental disabilities and their families, including autistic adults.
providers.services: Self-advocacy, independent-living support, benefits navigation, employment support, and connections to disability services.
providers.access: Visit the Common Ground resource desk and ask for an intake conversation about your goals and support needs.

providers.name: Stapleton Community Legal Aid
providers.audience: Residents with limited income who need civil legal assistance.
providers.services: Screening for eviction, housing conditions, benefits appeals, family safety, and other civil legal issues. Representation depends on eligibility and capacity.
providers.access: Ask the legal-aid intake desk about the relevant civil issue and any hearing or filing deadline. Do not post documents or identifying case details here.

providers.name: Neighborhood Family Resource Exchange
providers.audience: Families needing basic supplies or help navigating assistance.
providers.services: Diapers, period supplies, household essentials when stocked, and help finding utility and family-support programs.
providers.access: Ask the Family Resource Exchange welcome desk what supplies are currently available and about assistance with utility applications.
providers.hours: Walk-ins: Monday, Wednesday, and Friday, 10 AM–4 PM.

providers.name: Stapleton VA Outpatient Clinic
providers.audience: Veterans seeking information about VA health-care eligibility, enrollment, and services.
providers.services: Enrollment guidance, primary-care access, and referrals through the VA health-care system. This is a government health service, not a nonprofit.
providers.access: Ask the clinic enrollment and patient-services desk about eligibility, required enrollment documents, and appointment options. Pericles has no direct transfer or appointment-booking connection.
providers.hours: Enrollment desk: Monday–Friday, 8 AM–4:30 PM. Clinical appointments are scheduled separately.

rules: These are authored Stapleton scenario services, not verified real-world providers. Never invent phone numbers, street addresses, websites, live openings, clinical credentials, or completed referrals. Do not repeat scenario disclaimers to patrons.
Service hours are regular scheduled hours, not live availability. Shelter beds, treatment spaces, pantry stock, and enrollment must be confirmed by provider intake.
Do not diagnose, recommend an individual treatment, or give detox instructions. Direct medical withdrawal questions to a licensed clinician.
Never ask for identifying information, abuse details, medical records, or benefit documents in chat. Do not imply that Pericles contacts providers or books places.
Keep help practical and nonjudgmental. Do not use fee enforcement or unrelated library promotions in community-support responses.
